title: Lesson 17 - Discovery Workshops: Stakeholder Mapping and Requirements Capture
description: Conduct discovery workshops, analyze business requirements, define solutions, and prioritize use cases.

questions.question: During a workshop a department head says the new system must work exactly like the old one. What have you actually captured?
options: A confirmed functional requirement you can build to
A solution preference that hides the real requirement, so you keep asking why until you reach the underlying outcome
questions.explanation: A statement about the old system is a proposed solution, not an outcome, so the correct move is to keep asking why until the business need it protects is exposed; treating it as a functional requirement locks an old workaround into the new build.

questions.question: Which elicitation technique gives you the most reliable view of how work actually happens, as opposed to how people say it happens?
options: Shadowing an end user through a full transaction
A survey emailed to the team
questions.explanation: Observing a real transaction exposes workarounds and exceptions that people do not self-report, which is why the more physical and specific the technique, the closer it sits to truth; surveys and documentation both capture the official story.

questions.question: On a stakeholder map, what does an unengaged high-power stakeholder represent?
options: A low priority contact who can be dropped from updates
A risk to the project who needs a targeted engagement plan
An end user who will adopt automatically once the system ships
A sponsor by virtue of their seniority alone
questions.explanation: High power and low interest is the quadrant a project must keep satisfied, so an unengaged high-power stakeholder is a risk requiring a targeted engagement plan; seniority alone does not make someone the sponsor, which is a role the client names.
